rows.system: In an ultra-high-vacuum cryogenic ion trap, an isolated, stationary carbon-5+ ion (C⁵⁺) is prepared in an excited Bohr orbit. The hydrogenic ion spontaneously relaxes to the ground level by emitting a single extreme-ultraviolet photon, imparting a momentum kick to the nucleus and generating a measurable recoil velocity.

wavelength of the spectral line (nm) — 1/λ = R_H Z² (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²)
energy of one photon (eV) — E = hc/λ = 1240/λ(nm) eV

rows.system: A high-precision isoperibol bomb calorimeter is loaded with a pellet of crystalline azulene (C10H8) and pressurized with excess pure oxygen gas to determine its thermodynamic parameters via complete combustion. Following ignition, the temperature rise of the water bath is recorded to calculate the total heat evolved and the constant-volume internal energy change of combustion. Combining this with standard enthalpies of formation of gaseous CO2 and liquid H2O alongside theoretical bond enthalpy summation allows the determination of the aromatic resonance stabilization energy of the bicyclic non-alternant hydrocarbon.
formulas: resonance energy (kJ mol⁻¹) — ΔH_res = ΔfH(exp) − ΔfH(calc)
enthalpy of atomization per mole of atoms (kJ mol⁻¹) — ΔH_a per mole of X atoms = ½ BDE(X₂)
standard enthalpy of formation of the species (kJ mol⁻¹) — ΔrH = ΣνΔfH(products) − ΣνΔfH(reactants), solved for the one unknown
enthalpy of the target reaction (kJ mol⁻¹) — Hess: combine the equations; ΔH combines the same way

rows.system: A high-pressure, thermally insulated beryllium-copper cell containing dense xenon gas undergoes a reversible adiabatic expansion against a computer-controlled piston. The non-ideal behavior of xenon across this density regime is modeled by the truncated virial equation of state with a temperature-dependent second virial coefficient B(T). As the gas performs mechanical work against the piston, its compressibility and thermodynamic state evolve simultaneously.
not_in_list: virial_coefficient: second virial coefficient B (L mol⁻¹)
work: work done on the gas (J)

rows.system: In a high-precision volumetric gas sorption analyzer, an outgassed sample of ultra-microporous metal-organic framework (MOF-74-Ni) with a known specific surface area is exposed to a dosed aliquot of krypton gas at 120 K. As the system reaches physisorption equilibrium, real-gas non-ideality corrections are applied to the non-adsorbed krypton remaining in the sample cell dead volume to determine the monolayer packing density.
not_in_list: virial_coefficient: second virial coefficient B (L mol⁻¹)
molecular_area: surface area occupied by one molecule (m²)

rows.system: In a high-precision, steady-state radial flow Joule-Thomson porous plug calorimeter, high-purity compressed argon gas is continuously throttled through an insulated sintered silumin disc from an initial elevated pressure to an exhaust chamber. High-accuracy platinum resistance thermometers and differential piezoresistive pressure transducers measure the isenthalpic temperature and pressure changes across the plug to determine real-gas thermodynamic departures from ideality.
formulas: Joule-Thomson inversion temperature (K) — T_i = 2a/(bR); cooling on expansion below T_i
compressibility factor Z — low P: Z = 1 − a/(V_m RT) ≈ 1 − aP/(RT)²; high P: Z = 1 + Pb/RT
Boyle temperature (K) — T_B = a/(bR)

rows.system: In a sealed, constant-volume fused-silica high-temperature spectrophotometric cell equipped with a diaphragm pressure sensor, an initial dose of pure sulfuryl chloride (SO2Cl2) gas is heated to 375 K. The gas homogeneously dissociates into sulfur dioxide (SO2) and molecular chlorine (Cl2) until a steady thermodynamic equilibrium state is established. The resulting equilibrium mixture's total pressure and standard thermodynamic reaction parameters are measured to characterize the gas-phase dissociation.

rows.system: A synthesized specimen of non-stoichiometric wüstite (Fe_{1-x}O) exhibiting cation vacancy defects is prepared via high-temperature equilibration under a controlled CO/CO2 buffer gas mixture. The fraction of iron(III) and the non-stoichiometric empirical formula are determined by anaerobic acid dissolution followed by potentiometric redox titration of Fe2+ with a standard cerium(IV) solution, while the cubic unit cell parameter is characterized by powder X-ray diffraction.

A deaerated, thermostatted Harned-type electrochemical cell without liquid junction, configured as Pt(s) | H2(g, 1.00 bar) | chloroacetic acid (m1), sodium chloroacetate (m2), NaCl (m3) | AgCl(s) | Ag(s), is monitored across a temperature range of 288.15 K to 318.15 K to determine buffer ionization and cell reaction thermodynamics. High-frequency AC impedance is concurrently measured across twin platinized electrodes immersed in the cell chamber to determine solution resistance and electrolyte transport properties.

rows.system: A high-pressure variable-volume optical piezometer cell contains a known mass of purified gaseous ethane (C₂H₆) immersed in a precision silicone oil thermostat. As the calibrated piston adjusts the internal cell volume at a constant supercritical temperature, high-resolution pressure transducers record the non-ideal p-V-T response to characterize intermolecular interactions via the virial equation of state.

rows.system: In an isotopic enrichment pilot plant, a binary gaseous mixture of sulfur hexafluoride isotopologues (32SF6 and 34SF6) is continuously fed at low pressure into a multi-stage separation cell equipped with track-etched silicon nitride nanoporous membranes. The gas stream is maintained under isothermal conditions where the nanopore diameter is substantially smaller than the mean free path, ensuring pure Knudsen effusion across each stage. Measurements of downstream enrichment and gas properties quantify the efficiency of the isotopic separation process.

molar_mass: input of: ratio of the effusion rates r₁/r₂

rows.system: In an industrial wastewater treatment pilot unit for semiconductor fabrication effluent, an aqueous waste stream containing dilute hydrofluoric acid (HF) is neutralized with a sodium acetate/acetic acid buffer system and subsequently dosed with a concentrated calcium chloride (CaCl2) solution to selectively precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2). The reactor is maintained under controlled isothermal conditions at 25.0 °C to establish multi-equilibrium speciation between weak acid dissociation, common-ion buffering, and metal fluoride saturation.

rows.system: In an analytical biopharmaceutical laboratory, an aqueous formulation containing a synthetic therapeutic decapeptide and sodium chloride excipient is prepared to assess concentration-dependent self-association into dimeric complexes. A known mass of the lyophilized peptide is dissolved in a volumetric flask with degassed ultrapure water of known density, and the resulting dilute solution is transferred to a thermostatted membrane osmometer operating at 298.15 K to record the equilibrium osmotic pressure against pure solvent across a semipermeable membrane.

In a sealed, rigid nickel-alloy autoclave of known internal volume, a pure sample of sulfuryl chloride vapour is heated to 375 K, undergoing homogeneous gas-phase thermal dissociation into sulfur dioxide and chlorine gas. Once thermodynamic equilibrium is established, the total pressure and mixture density are measured via an in-situ high-temperature piezoresistive transducer and a vibrating-tube densimeter to determine the extent of decomposition.
not_in_list: gas_density: density of the gas (g L⁻¹)

rows.system: In a Burnett isothermal expansion apparatus, a high-purity gaseous sample of octafluorocyclobutane (c-C4F8) is expanded through an automated expansion valve from a primary charge chamber into an evacuated secondary chamber maintained at a constant temperature of 360 K. High-precision quartz Bourdon pressure transducers and volumetric calibration are used to track the stepwise pressure drop and molar volume across consecutive expansions to characterize the gas-phase intermolecular potentials.

rows.system: A pristine, micro-drilled monazite crystal extracted from a deep Precambrian granulite-facies metamorphic complex is analyzed using high-resolution isotope dilution mass spectrometry to determine radiogenic lead accumulation from the uranium-238 decay chain. Assuming the mineral has remained a closed system devoid of initial non-radiogenic lead since crystallization, the isotopic composition and total alpha-decay history are modeled from the measured isotopic inventories.

In an extractive metallurgy assay laboratory, an accurately weighed mineral sample of commercial pyrolusite ore containing manganese dioxide (MnO2) and inert siliceous gangue is digested in hot dilute sulfuric acid with a known volumetric excess of standardized sodium oxalate (Na2C2O4) solution. After complete reductive dissolution of the manganese(IV) oxide, the unconsumed oxalate remaining in the acidic digest is back-titrated at 70 °C against a standardized potassium permanganate (KMnO4) solution to determine the active mineral grade.

rows.system: In an automated volumetric gas sorption apparatus, an outgassed sample of ultra-stable Y (USY) zeolite is equilibrated with dry krypton gas maintained at 77.35 K across a range of sub-atmospheric pressures. The equilibrium partial pressure and corresponding mass uptake per unit adsorbent mass (extent of adsorption, x/m) are monitored across the sub-monolayer regime to determine monolayer saturation and evaluate the effective cross-sectional packing of the adsorbate on the microporous framework.

In an aerospace propulsion ground-test facility, a gaseous binary working fluid of helium and xenon with a calibrated molar composition is sealed in a heavily insulated, instrumented piston-cylinder device. The gas mixture undergoes a reversible polytropic expansion from an initial high-pressure reservoir state to a designated discharge volume, delivering shaft work to a precision dynamometer.
